clue.text: Blocks half of loch, having unfortunately sunk

indicators.note: only the first half of the word loch is taken, its opening two letters
something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters of sunk are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Something has sunk in a Scottish lake, and the obstacle is half the loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes CH from loch; 'unfortunately' rearranges SUNK into UNKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chunks are solid lumps or pieces, which is what blocks of material are.

clue.text: End of food chain taking on the Spanish officer?

parts.note: the colon is the last stretch of the gut, the end of the chain that food passes along
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Some officer at the top of the food chain picks up a Spanish article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'food chain' suggests ecology, but here it is the digestive tract, whose end is the colon.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior military rank, so an example of an officer, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Cruel twist, a source of pain

indicators.note: a twist wrings the word Cruel out of shape, so its five letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A cruel turn of events brings someone pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' rearranges CRUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is a painful sore, so it is something that causes pain.

clue.text: Sovereign state puts family first, God out and men last

parts.note: kin means family, relatives

indicators.note: out signals the word God is put out of its usual order

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for male, standing for men here

explanation.surface: A royal realm sets out its order: family first, God dismissed, men at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GOD into GDO. 'first' and 'last' just place KIN at the start and M at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is a country ruled by a monarch, a state with a sovereign at its head.

clue.text: Reinforce rise in price of steak

definitions.meaning: read literally, beef going up in cost

explanation.definitionFit: To beef up is an idiom for making something stronger, and literally it reads as beef rising.

clue.text: Mistakes made by deserter in time

indicators.note: in places the deserter word inside the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is someone who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: Errors made by a soldier who went AWOL at some point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserter' hints at a soldier, but it is the rodent word for a turncoat; 'in' does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed errors in a printed work, so they are mistakes.

clue.text: FBI agent appraised after English formed an alliance

indicators.note: after places the word for appraised following the English abbreviation

parts.note: a fed is US slang for a federal agent such as one from the FBI
rated means assessed or appraised

explanation.surface: An FBI agent, having been sized up after an English contact, teamed up with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts RATED after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Federated means joined together in a federation, a league or alliance.

clue.text: Piper suffering from flamboyance?

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god who plays the pipes
an ache is a pain, a form of suffering

explanation.surface: A bagpiper in some distress is accused of showiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piper' suggests a bagpiper or the Pied Piper, but it is the pipe-playing god Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is dashing style and swagger, close to flamboyance.

clue.text: Bounty man to choose what's needed for a baptism

parts.note: Fletcher Christian led the mutiny on HMS Bounty
to name is to select or nominate

explanation.surface: A man of the Bounty picks out what a christening requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounty man' sounds like a bounty hunter; it is Fletcher Christian, leader of the 1789 mutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: At a baptism the child is given its first, given name, traditionally called this.

clue.text: A beer and cold Guinness?

parts.note: ale is a beer
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone orders a beer and a cold glass of Guinness stout.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinness looks like the stout, but it is the actor Sir Alec Guinness.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec Guinness was a famous British actor, so the forename is an example of a Guinness.

clue.text: "Noah's out" (modern dance) — okay!

indicators.note: letters made to dance are jumbled into a new arrangement
out says the letter of the possessive is put out of the name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone announces Noah's exit, with a modern dance, and all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops S from NOAHS; 'dance' rearranges NOAH and MODERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no harm was done reassures that all is fine, an idiomatic equivalent of okay.

clue.text: Bergman seen here?

definitions.meaning: something in a crossword is in the grid, split as two words

explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the actress Bergman, and a phrase locating something within this crossword's grid.

clue.text: Operate reciprocally with Virgin Queen inside

indicators.note: inside places the Queen abbreviation within the word for virgin

parts.note: intact can mean virginal, untouched
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Something works both ways with the Virgin Queen, Elizabeth I, inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin Queen' reads as Elizabeth I but must be split into two separate pieces; 'inside' does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: To interact is to act on one another, which is operating reciprocally.

clue.text: Inform a friend?

parts.note: read as in-form, a friend from the same school form, not as passing on news

explanation.definitionFit: A pupil in the same form at school is a school friend in your class.

clue.text: He clears the way while getting over shell shock

indicators.note: a shock jolts the letters of the two words into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man clears a path while recovering from the trauma of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shell shock' reads as war trauma, but 'shock' rearranges OVER and SHELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoveller digs and clears with a shovel, as when shifting snow from a path.

clue.text: Last year's ailment

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: the phrase has the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: An illness someone suffered last year.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 's as 'has': 'Last year' holds the letters running across the word gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a minor ailment.

clue.text: Sell when game to come back

indicators.note: coming back means the word for the game is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: golf is a game

explanation.surface: Someone sells up when a game is about to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come back' reverses GOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: Flog is British slang for selling something, especially cheaply or aggressively.

clue.text: Quadripartite key to the Guardian's style?

parts.note: F is a musical key
our, as the newspaper setting the puzzle refers to itself
a way is a manner or style

explanation.surface: A newspaper's house style is said to be the key to splitting things four ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's paper speaks of itself: the Guardian's is OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Quadripartite means having four parts or parties, the same as involving four sides.

clue.text: Nurse endlessly transmits to mobile receivers

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to care for is to nurse
radios means sends by radio, transmits

explanation.surface: A nurse keeps sending messages to someone's mobile phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from CARE, leaving CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sets fitted in motor vehicles pick up broadcasts on the move, mobile receivers.

clue.text: Rubbish reportedly beneath bandstand

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for beneath is given as it sounds in speech

parts.note: under means beneath

explanation.surface: Litter has been reported lying under the bandstand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' says UNDER is given as pronounced, non-rhotically, UNDA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building with a domed roof, a shape often used for a bandstand.

clue.text: Where table napkin is placed to extend beyond the edge

definitions.meaning: a diner spreads the napkin over the thighs
to jut out past a boundary and cover part of something

explanation.definitionFit: A napkin goes over your lap, and to jut past an edge onto something is to overlap.

clue.text: Creator of Andy Capp's a legend in one corner of England

indicators.note: in places the word for a legend within the corner abbreviation

parts.note: SE, the South East, is a corner of England
a myth is a legend

explanation.surface: The cartoonist behind Andy Capp is a local legend in a corner of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Capp is a long-running British newspaper cartoon about a workshy northern layabout; 'in' does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Reg Smythe drew the Andy Capp comic strip for the Daily Mirror from 1957.

clue.text: He engineered changes in telephone boxes

definitions.text: He engineered changes in telephone boxes

parts.words: He engineered changes in telephone boxes
parts.note: not an engineer at the telephone company but a hero who changes his clothes in phone booths

explanation.definitionFit: Clark Kent famously switches into his superhero costume inside a phone booth.

clue.text: Non-drinker keeps fit with this pill

indicators.note: keeps means the non-drinker abbreviation holds the word for fit within it

parts.note: TT means teetotal, a non-drinker
able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: A teetotaller stays healthy by taking this pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-drinker' is the teetotaller, a common crossword abbreviation; 'keeps' does the holding.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a small solid dose of medicine, the same as a pill.

clue.text: Leaf taken from shortened male version of "Sister Act"?

parts.note: the male counterpart of sister is brother, abbreviated to Br
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leaf is lifted from a cut-down male take on the film Sister Act.
explanation.walkthrough: The male version of the film title would be Brother Act; brother shortened is BR.
explanation.definitionFit: A bract is a modified leaf beneath a flower, so it is a kind of leaf.

clue.text: He's fractionally not quite inside, we hear

definitions.text: He's fractionally not quite inside, we hear

parts.words: He's fractionally not quite inside, we hear
parts.note: a cricket reserve: one beyond the eleven players, a fraction title, and just outside the team

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the twelfth man is the reserve who is not in the playing eleven but fields as a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket reserve, numbered one past the eleven, is just outside the team.

clue.text: It helps to keep the rotor turning, as chopper hovers over Laotian capital

definitions.text: It helps to keep the rotor turning

indicators.note: the chopper word hovers over, so surrounds, the capital letter

parts.note: an axe is a chopping tool, a chopper

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A helicopter hovers over the capital of Laos while its rotor turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' suggests a helicopter but is AXE; 'capital' takes L from Laotian, held inside AXE.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the shaft about which a wheel or rotor spins.

clue.text: Ready to move outside, first of nominees kept on chatting

indicators.note: outside puts the jumbled word around the single letter
making the letters move rearranges the word Ready
the first letter of the word nominees

explanation.surface: Nominees, ready to move outside, kept talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges READY into YARED; 'outside' wraps it round N from 'first of nominees'.
explanation.definitionFit: To yarn is to tell long stories or chat at length, so yarned means kept on talking.

clue.text: Student gets suitable work via computer

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver
apt means suitable
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A student gets decent work done on a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on British cars, so it stands for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable computer.
